title: Transfer Price Lock for Recently Transferred-In Domains — Domain Registrations Restore-Day Extensions
content:
**Price lock terms — Domain Registrations**

A domain that came to Harborline by an inbound transfer keeps part of its transfer price on extension years ordered on its restore day: the restore-day transfer price lock is one of the restore-day credits.

### Terms

The restore-day transfer price lock, one of the restore-day credits, is the amount by which the TLD's renewal price exceeds its inbound transfer price, for each of the restore-day years, where the domain came to Harborline by an inbound transfer completed less than 12 whole months before the day of the order, that difference once for the order where the inbound transfer completed at least 12 but less than 24 whole months before it, and nothing otherwise or where the renewal price does not exceed the transfer price.

### Ladder by age of the inbound transfer

| Inbound transfer completed before the day of the order | Price lock |
|---|---|
| less than 12 whole months | the renewal price less the transfer price, for each restore-day year |
| at least 12 but less than 24 whole months | the renewal price less the transfer price, once |
| 24 whole months or more, or the domain was newly registered | nothing |
| any age, renewal price not above the transfer price | nothing |

The age is counted in whole months from the date the inbound transfer completed to the day of the order, a month counting only once its day of the month is reached.

### Hypothetical cases (invented prices: renewal USD 40.00, transfer USD 36.00)

- Transfer completed 10 March 2027, order 9 March 2028 (11 whole months), 3 restore-day years: USD 4.00 for each year, USD 12.00.
- Same transfer, order 10 March 2028 (12 whole months), 3 restore-day years: USD 4.00 once.
- Same transfer, order 10 March 2029 (24 whole months): nothing.
- Renewal price USD 35.00 against a transfer price of USD 36.00: nothing at any age.
